title: Improving Irrigation Regimes and Plant Spacing to Maximize Rice Grain Yield and Water Productivity
authors: Hasnaa A. Ghazy; B. B. Mikhael; I. S. El-Refaee
location_name: Experimental Farm, Sakha Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh, Egypt
methods_summary: Seasons [2017, 2018]; cultivar Giza 179; 30-day seedlings; sowing dates {'2017': '2017-05-13', '2018': '2018-05-15'}; N=165 kg/ha; clayey soil; water measured with calibrated water meter.
limitations: Small experimental station plots with three replications; results are not representative farmer-field observations. The paper reports treatment water productivity but the extracted tables do not provide absolute seasonal applied-water volumes by treatment. Do not convert these results directly into pump run-time recommendations without local pump discharge and field calibration. Yield results are influenced by the study's cultivar, clayey soil, seedling age, spacing, fertilizer package, and trial management.

title: Effect of soil puddling and previous crop on some soil properties and rice productivity in clay soils
location_name: Faculty of Agriculture farm, Kafrelsheikh University; experiment season 2007
methods_summary: Four fields; Giza 177 rice; preceding crops wheat or Egyptian clover; puddling vs no puddling; three replicates; soil sampled at 0-30 and 30-60 cm.
limitations: Single research-farm site and one season; grouped treatment means rather than plot-level records; not a field-specific soil test or current universal recommendation.

title: Effects of Soil Fertilization on Sakha 105 Rice Cultivar Productivity, NPK Uptake and Soil Nutrient
authors: E. E. Gewaily; A. M. Ghoneim; Howida B. I. Elhabet
location_name: Rice Research and Training Center experimental farm, Sakha, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Published pre-plant soil baseline for 2016 and 2017 rice fertilizer trials; four experimental replicates.
limitations: One station/site; no parcel-specific sampling coordinates or sampling depth reported in the table; baseline values are not a current farmer soil test and do not establish nutrient sufficiency thresholds.

title: Effects of Previous Rice Cropping History on Salt Accumulation of Surface Soils in the Middle Nile Delta, Egypt
authors: Y. Yageta; T. Higashi; Z. A. Bassiouni; N. El Sayed Saad; M. Satoh
location_name: 15 study sites within 5 km of the Rice Research and Training Center, Sakha, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Soil and irrigation-water samples from one ARC site and 14 nearby private farms; sites grouped by rice cultivation frequency during the two preceding years; soil sampled at 0-20 cm in May 2010.
limitations: Small observational study from 2010 with grouped site comparisons; no public parcel-level coordinates or farmer-level raw table. The result is specific to the sampled area and drainage/water conditions.

title: Effect of preceding winter crops and biological fertilization on growth and yield of rice under different levels of nitrogen fertilization
location_name: Tag El-Ezz Agricultural Research Station, Dakahlia Governorate (neighboring Delta; not Kafr El-Sheikh)
methods_summary: Sakha 101 rice; summers 2000 and 2001; berseem vs wheat preceding crop; nitrogen and Cyriallen treatments; four replications.
limitations: Not conducted in Kafr El-Sheikh; older station experiment; treatment means cannot be transferred as current field-specific soil tests or fertilizer doses.

title: Rice varieties as affected with different irrigation periods and submerged depths in the North Nile Delta region
authors: R. Kh. Darwesh; A. A. Abdelkhalek; M. A. M. Ibrahim
location_name: Sakha Agricultural Research Station Farm, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Two seasons (2013, 2014); intervals 6/12 days; ponding depths 3/5/7 cm; Giza 177, Sakha 101, Orabi 1; water measured by rectangular weir; 3 replications; treatment means transcribed from Tables 1-4.
limitations: Single research-station site and historical seasons. No parcel-specific prediction. Seasonal applied water includes nursery, land preparation, and establishment water. Irrigation depths/intervals are experimental treatments, not prescriptions for every farm.

title: Water Requirement Components of some Egyptian Rice Varieties in North Nile Delta
authors: E. A. Moursi; A. A. Abdelkhalek
location_name: Sakha Agricultural Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Two experiments in summer 2012 and 2013; Giza 178, Sakha 102, Sakha 104; measured actual ETa with micro-paddy lysimeter; estimated ETo by Hargreaves, Penman-Monteith, Class A pan; irrigation water balance and seasonal productivity.
limitations: Research station only, not farmer labels. Mixes season-specific climate summaries and two-season mean treatment summaries. Rainfall/drainage/runoff/seepage treated as negligible or unavailable in the study water budget. Wind-speed unit is inconsistent between table and narrative and is preserved as ambiguous. Values transcribed from tables/results; do not use directly as parcel or pump-run-time recommendations.

title: Role of Composted Rice Straw and Potassium Silicate in Improving Productivity of Sakha 106 Rice Cultivar with Raised Water Use Efficiency
authors: Hasnaa A. Ghazy; I. M. Hashem; I. A. Sheta
location_name: Experimental Farm, Sakha Agriculture Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Rice seasons 2022 and 2023; Sakha 106; irrigation every 4, 8, and 12 days; 3 replications; factorial compost/potassium-silicate treatments. Table 8 contains irrigation-interval marginal means.
limitations: Station experiment only. Table 8 values are marginal means across fertilizer combinations; not individual fertilizer-treatment outcomes and not farmer observations. Irrigation totals cannot be converted to pump run times without a farm duty point. Verify transcribed values and method context against the PDF before operational use.

title: Planting Methods and Irrigation Depth Management to Enhance Water Productivity and Yield of Rice in the Northern Nile Delta, Egypt
authors: Mona S. M. Eid; Ibrahim M. Abdel-Fattah; Mai A. M. Elsaka; Hesham M. Abo-Elsoud
location_name: Northern Nile Delta, Egypt; exact station/location not confirmed in this extract
methods_summary: Factorial study, seasons 2023 and 2024; traditional/furrow/bed planting × 7/5/3 cm water depth. Table 3 reports irrigation water, grain yield, and irrigation water productivity treatment means.
limitations: Regional Northern Nile Delta paper. Exact field/station location, cultivar, and replication count were not carried into this extracted table record; do not spatially assign it to a Kafr El-Sheikh parcel. These are trial treatment means, not farmer labels or pump runtime instructions.

title: Effect of Water Deficit at Critical Physiological Stages of Rice on WUE and Productivity
methods_summary: Field experiment in the 2014 and 2015 summer seasons; continuous flooding compared with 12-day water withholding at mid-tillering, panicle initiation, or heading. Table 8 reports seasonal treatment means.
limitations: Station treatment means, not farm records. Table 8 values are irrigation-treatment means across three cultivars; they cannot estimate a specific parcel, cultivar, or pump runtime. The table reports water saving 6.33% for 2014 W_MT; the abstract prints 6.37%, so the table value is retained and the discrepancy is documented.

title: Evaluation rice varieties under different sowing dates and planting methods
location_name: Sakha Agriculture Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Two summer-season experiments (2012, 2013); varieties/lines GZ 7112, GZ 9057 and Sakha 105; sowing dates 15 April, 1 May and 15 May; transplanting and drill sowing.
limitations: Only abstract values transcribed; GZ 9057 result is from a DUS experiment and is not a commercial farmer-field yield guarantee.

title: Impact of Various Irrigation Water Types on Soil Quality, Grain Heavy Metals Concentration and Productivity of Some Rice Varieties
authors: A. A. Gaber; Amira M. Okasha; M. M. Abdelhamed; B. A. Zayed
location_name: Sakha Agriculture Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Two summer-season field trials (2022 and 2023), strip-plot design with four replicates; FW, DW, 1FW:1DW, 2FW:1DW, 1FW:2DW; Giza 183, Giza 178, Sakha 106 and Sakha 108. Tables 10-14 transcribed.
limitations: Water chemistry and soil chemical/metal tables remain untranscribed. Grain concentrations are experimental treatment means, not a food-safety determination, universal blend recommendation or farmer-field prediction.

title: Irrigation Water Management of Rice Crop in North Delta
authors: E. M. El-Hadidi; M. E. Meleha; M. A. A. Elbialy
location_name: El-Karada Water Requirements Research Station, Kafr El-Sheikh
methods_summary: Two summer seasons (2006, 2007); Sakha 104; randomized complete block with three replicates; six transplanting layouts; irrigation water volume and grain yield reported.
limitations: Research-station trial, not farm observations or a current universal recommendation. Tables were transcribed from indexed author-copy/full-text; do not conflate with another similarly themed Meleha et al. study.

title: Effect of Irrigation with Drainage and Blended Waters on Yield and Quality of some Rice Varieties (Oryza sativa) as well as Soil Quality at North Part of Nile Delta
authors: Mona S. M. Eid; I. M. Abdel-Fattah; Amira M. Okasha
location_name: Hammoul District, North Nile Delta, Egypt
methods_summary: Two seasons (2020 and 2021); three rice cultivars (Sakha 104, Giza 177, Giza 178); irrigation treatments: agricultural drainage water, alternating drainage and blended canal water, and blended canal water.
limitations: The transcribed soil and water chemistry are published experimental-site values, not parcel-level measurements. These tables do not establish each farmer pump runtime or an operational safe-use prescription. Table 5 has conflicting soil EC reporting and was excluded.

title: Creating digital maps for geotechnical characteristics of soil based on GIS technology and remote sensing
authors: Mohammed A. El-Banna; Ali M. Basha; Ashraf A. A. Beshr
methods_summary: 119 geotechnical soil borings, laboratory tests, and modified inverse-distance-weighted interpolation; groundwater depths monitored during boring and after 24 hours; published Table 1 reports interpolated area by depth class.
limitations: This is a geotechnical map summary, not parcel-level agricultural groundwater monitoring. The article reports a mapped area (3835.461 km2) that differs from its stated governorate area (3716.68 km2); use only as coarse contextual reference, never as a field-specific value.

title: Role of Irrigation Intervals and Plant Spacing on Growth, Yield and its Components for some Rice Cultivated Varieties
authors: I. A. Sheta; S. A. Soltan; Amany K. Elhabbak
location_name: Rice Research and Training Center, Sakha, Kafr El-Sheikh, Egypt
methods_summary: Two summer field seasons (2019 and 2020), strip-split plot, four replications; Giza 179 and Sakha 106; irrigation continuous flooding, 6-day or 12-day interval; spacing 15x20, 20x20, 25x20 cm. Abstract-level transcription only.
limitations: Only qualitative conclusions entered from publisher abstract. Treatment-level yield and applied-water tables were not transcribed; results are from station plots and do not define a universal irrigation schedule or pump runtime.

title: Influence of Sowing Dates and Nitrogen Fertilization Levels on Rice Yield and Insect Infestation of Sakha Super 300 Rice Cultivar
authors: A. S. Taha; H. A. Saleh; Eman M. Bleih
location_name: Rice Research and Training Center, Sakha, Kafr El-Sheikh, Egypt
methods_summary: Two station field seasons (2019, 2020); Sakha Super 300; sowing dates May 1, June 1, July 1; nitrogen rates 0, 46, 69, 92 kg N/feddan; preceding crop wheat; 30-day seedlings; 20x20 cm spacing; 3 replicates per treatment reported in methods. Full-text tables/abstract text reviewed; only results captured in literature_evidence.
limitations: Research station treatment results, not farmer-field labels. Cultivar, season, fertilizer and management specific. Historical herbicide use in paper is not a current legal product recommendation. Do not generalize one trial to all varieties or seasons.

title: Estimating the Technological and Economic Efficiency of Some Improved Varieties for Rice Crop Production in Kafr El-Sheikh Governorate
authors: Wael Ahmed Ezzat ElAbd; Fathia Farid Abdullah; Salwa Mohamed Ahmed Abdelmoneam
methods_summary: University repository abstract describes a Data Envelopment Analysis of rice production resources for Sakha 101, Giza 178 and Giza 177, comparing technological/economic efficiency and potential input savings. Underlying field-level records and sample size are not exposed in the repository abstract.
limitations: Abstract-level transcription from university repository; efficiency and water-savings are model-derived, not observed measured savings for each farm. The reported 1539 m3 has no clear denominator in the abstract; do not scale it per feddan or use for runtime calculations.
